MAVUNO TEXTILES LIMITED
COMMERCIAL FIRE AND SPECIAL PERILS INSURANCE POLICY Insurer: Amani General Insurance Company Limited
Policy Number: AGI/FIRE/2025/00842
Insured: Mavuno Textiles Limited
Risk Address: Plot 14, Kariobangi Industrial Area, Nairobi, Kenya
Occupancy/Use: Textile manufacturing (spinning, weaving, dyeing and garment finishing)
Period of Insurance: 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2026 SECTION A: PROPERTY INSURED Item 1 - Buildings (factory shed, dye house, warehouse, administration block) Sum Insured: KES 220,000,000 Item 2 - Plant and Machinery (spinning frames, looms, dyeing vats, boilers, generators) Sum Insured: KES 180,000,000

Item 3 - Stock (raw cotton, yarn, finished garments, packaging materials) Sum Insured: KES 90,000,000 Total Sum Insured: KES 490,000,000 SECTION B: PERILS COVERED This Policy covers loss or damage to the Property Insured caused by: 1. Fire 2. Lightning 3. Explosion (domestic boilers and gas only, unless extended) 4. Aircraft and other aerial devices 5. Riot, strike and malicious damage 6. Storm, tempest, flood 7. Impact by vehicles SECTION C: EXCLUSIONS

This Policy does not cover: 1. Loss or damage caused by the insured's own wilful act or gross negligence. 2. Loss or damage arising from war, invasion, act of foreign enemy, civil war, or terrorism, unless specifically bought back by endorsement. 3. Loss or damage where the Insured has failed to maintain the fire protection and safety measures declared at inception (see Warranty 1 below). 4. Consequential loss, including loss of profits, business interruption, or loss of market, unless separately insured under a Business Interruption Policy. 5

. Loss or damage to electrical machinery caused by over-running, excessive pressure, short circuiting, self-heating or leakage of electricity, unless fire ensues, in which case only the ensuing fire damage is covered. 6. Loss or damage occurring while the premises are left unoccupied for a continuous period exceeding 30 days, unless declared and agreed by the Insurer in writing. 7. Fines, penalties, or punitive damages of any kind. 8. Loss discovered more than 30 days after the Insured first became aware, or ought reasonably to have become aware, of circumstances giving rise to a claim, unless late notification is excused in writing by the Insurer.
SECTION D: WARRANTIES

Warranty 1 (Fire Protection Warranty): It is warranted that the Insured shall, at all
times during the currency of this Policy, maintain in good working order: (a) a functioning automatic sprinkler system covering the dye house and warehouse; (b) portable fire extinguishers serviced within the preceding 12 months, positioned at intervals not exceeding 30 metres throughout the factory floor; (c) a fire hydrant system connected to a water reserve of not less than 50,000 litres; (d) an internal fire brigade or trained fire marshal team of not fewer than 6 persons per shift.
Breach of this Warranty, if material to the cause or extent of the loss, entitles the
Insurer to decline or reduce indemnity in respect of the affected claim.

Warranty 2 (Housekeeping Warranty): It is warranted that flammable waste (cotton
lint, thread ends, packaging offcuts) shall be removed from production areas at the
end of each working shift and stored in designated fire-resistant bins located at
least 15 metres from the main production floor. SECTION E: EXCESS/DEDUCTIBLE Each and every claim: KES 2,500,000, or 2% of the claim amount, whichever is greater. SECTION F: CONDITIONS PRECEDENT TO LIABILITY

SECTION F: CONDITIONS PRECEDENT TO LIABILITY 1. The Insured shall notify the Insurer within 14 days of any occurrence likely to give rise to a claim. 2. The Insured shall furnish all information and documentary evidence reasonably required by the Insurer, including invoices, stock records, and maintenance records for fire protection equipment. 3. The Insured shall take all reasonable steps to minimise or avert loss. 4. No admission, offer, promise, or payment shall be made by or on behalf of the Insured without the written consent of the Insurer. SECTION G: REINSURANCE NOTE (for internal cedant use)

SECTION G: REINSURANCE NOTE (for internal cedant use) This risk is ceded under the Amani General Insurance Company Limited Fire and Special
Perils Surplus Treaty with Kenya Reinsurance Corporation Limited, Treaty Reference
KR/AGI/SUR/2026, subject to the terms of that treaty. Any claim under this Policy
exceeding the cedant's retention shall be notified to Kenya Reinsurance Corporation
Limited within 14 days of the cedant becoming aware of it. Signed for and on behalf of Amani General Insurance Company Limited.

KENYA REINSURANCE CORPORATION LIMITED
FIRE AND SPECIAL PERILS SURPLUS REINSURANCE TREATY Treaty Reference: KR/AGI/SUR/2026
Reinsurer: Kenya Reinsurance Corporation Limited ("Kenya Re")
Cedant: Amani General Insurance Company Limited ("the Cedant")
Class of Business: Fire and Special Perils (Commercial and Industrial risks)
Treaty Type: Surplus (proportional)
Period: 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2026, and each anniversary thereafter unless
terminated in accordance with Article 14. ARTICLE 1 - SCOPE

ARTICLE 1 - SCOPE This Treaty covers the Cedant's Fire and Special Perils portfolio written in the
Republic of Kenya, including manufacturing, warehousing, commercial and industrial
occupancies, subject to the terms, conditions, limits and exclusions set out below. ARTICLE 2 - CEDANT'S RETENTION AND TREATY CAPACITY

ARTICLE 2 - CEDANT'S RETENTION AND TREATY CAPACITY 2.1 The Cedant's retention (Line) for any one risk is KES 50,000,000 of Sum Insured.
2.2 The Treaty provides 8 Lines of automatic surplus capacity, being KES 400,000,000 in excess of the Cedant's retention, giving total automatic capacity of KES 450,000,000 per risk.
2.3 Kenya Re participates on each risk ceded in the same proportion as the surplus amount bears to the total Sum Insured of that risk (the "Cession Percentage").
2.4 Kenya Re's share of any claim is calculated by applying the Cession Percentage to the amount of the claim payable by the Cedant under the original Policy, after deduction of the Policy excess.
ARTICLE 3 - RISKS REQUIRING ENHANCED ASSESSMENT

3.1 Any risk with a total Sum Insured exceeding KES 300,000,000 shall be classified as an Enhanced Assessment Risk.
3.2 For Enhanced Assessment Risks, the Cedant shall, prior to binding cover, provide Kenya Re with: (a) a detailed risk survey report not older than 24 months; (b) confirmation of fire protection measures in place; (c) loss history for the preceding 5 years; and (d) construction and occupancy details.
3.3 Underwriting guideline reference: Section 4.2 of the Kenya Re Underwriting Manual requires that Enhanced Assessment Risks be reviewed by a Senior Underwriter before automatic cession is confirmed, and that any risk with Sum Insured exceeding KES 400,000,000 be referred for facultative consideration outside this Treaty.
ARTICLE 4 - EXCLUSIONS UNDER THE TREATY

This Treaty excludes and Kenya Re shall have no liability in respect of: 4.1 War, invasion, act of foreign enemy, hostilities, civil war, rebellion, insurrection, or terrorism. 4.2 Nuclear risks of any kind. 4.3 Losses arising from the Cedant's failure to comply with a Warranty under the original Policy, where such failure is material to the loss. 4.4 Losses where the original Policy excess has not first been applied. 4.5 Business interruption or consequential loss, unless separately agreed by addendum to this Treaty. 4.6 Any risk bound by the Cedant in breach of the underwriting guidelines referenced in Article 3.3.
ARTICLE 5 - CLAIMS NOTIFICATION AND COOPERATION

5.1 The Cedant shall notify Kenya Re within 14 days of becoming aware of any claim or circumstance likely to involve this Treaty, and in any event immediately for any claim where the estimated gross loss exceeds KES 20,000,000.
5.2 The Cedant shall provide Kenya Re with all documentation reasonably required to assess the claim, including the claim form, original Policy, loss adjuster or investigation reports, invoices, photographs, and any other supporting evidence.
5.3 Kenya Re shall be entitled to appoint its own loss adjuster, at its own cost, to review any claim where the Cedant's estimated gross loss exceeds KES 50,000,000, or where Kenya Re reasonably consider

the Cedant's estimated gross loss exceeds KES 50,000,000, or where Kenya Re reasonably considers the claim to be unusual having regard to the Cedant's historical claims experience under this Treaty.
5.4 Claims shall be settled by the Cedant in accordance with the terms of the original Policy
. Kenya Re shall follow the fortunes of the Cedant, provided that the claim has been handled by the Cedant in good faith and in accordance with the terms of the original Policy and this Treaty.
ARTICLE 6 - CLAIMS REQUIRING PRIOR REFERRAL TO KENYA RE

6.1 Notwithstanding Article 5.4, the Cedant shall obtain Kenya Re's prior written agreement before settling any claim where: (a) the estimated gross loss exceeds KES 60,000,000; or (b) there is a reasonable suspicion of arson, fraud, or material misrepresentation at inception; or (c) the cause of loss, or the applicability of a Policy exclusion or Warranty, is genuinely in doubt; or (d) required documentation under the original Policy (including but not limited to fire investigation or loss adjuster reports) has not yet been furnished.
6.2 Where none of the conditions in Article 6.1 apply, and the claim is otherwise consistent with the Cedant's normal claims experience, the Cedant may proceed to settle the claim without further reference to Kenya Re, subject to Article 5.2.

ARTICLE 7 - PREMIUM AND COMMISSION Kenya Re shall receive its Cession Percentage of the original gross premium, less
a ceding commission of 30%, payable quarterly. ARTICLE 8 - CURRENCY All amounts under this Treaty are expressed in Kenya Shillings (KES) unless
otherwise stated. ARTICLE 9 - CATASTROPHE PROTECTION This Treaty operates net of the Cedant's own Catastrophe Excess of Loss
protection, where applicable. A single occurrence affecting multiple risks ceded
under this Treaty shall be aggregated for the purposes of any such protection.

ARTICLE 10 to 13 - [General conditions: arbitration, errors and omissions,
inspection of records, offset, taxation - standard treaty wording, on file with
both parties.] ARTICLE 14 - DURATION AND TERMINATION This Treaty renews annually unless either party gives not less than 3 months'
written notice prior to any anniversary date. Executed between the Cedant and Kenya Reinsurance Corporation Limited.

AMANI GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED
CLAIM FORM - FIRE AND SPECIAL PERILS Claim Reference: AGI/CLM/2026/1187
Policy Number: AGI/FIRE/2025/00842
Insured: Mavuno Textiles Limited
Risk Address: Plot 14, Kariobangi Industrial Area, Nairobi, Kenya 1. DETAILS OF LOSS Date of Loss: 3 August 2026
Time of Loss: Approximately 02:40 hrs
Date Reported to Insurer: 4 August 2026
Cause of Loss (as understood by Insured): Fire, believed to have started in the
dye house near the boiler room, spreading to the adjoining warehouse before being
brought under control by Nairobi County Fire Brigade at approximately 06:15 hrs. 2. DESCRIPTION OF INCIDENT

2. DESCRIPTION OF INCIDENT The night shift supervisor, Mr. Peter Kamau, reported smelling smoke at
approximately 02:35 hrs and raised the alarm. The internal fire marshal team
attempted to contain the fire using portable extinguishers but were unable to
control it due to its rapid spread through stored cotton lint in the warehouse
section adjoining the dye house. The Nairobi County Fire Brigade was called at
02:48 hrs and arrived on site at approximately 03:20 hrs. The fire was fully
extinguished by 06:15 hrs. No fatalities were reported. Two employees were treated
for smoke inhalation at Kenyatta National Hospital and discharged the same day. 3. ITEMS/PROPERTY AFFECTED

3. ITEMS/PROPERTY AFFECTED - Dye house structure and dyeing vats: substantially destroyed - Adjoining warehouse structure: significant fire and water damage - Stock (raw cotton, yarn, packaging materials) stored in warehouse: total loss - Finished garment stock in a separate, unaffected store: no damage reported - Administration block: minor smoke damage only - Spinning and weaving floor (separate building): no fire damage reported, minor smoke residue reported by the Insured, still being assessed 4. ESTIMATED CLAIM AMOUNT

4. ESTIMATED CLAIM AMOUNT Buildings (dye house and warehouse): KES 38,000,000 Plant and Machinery (dyeing vats, boilers): KES 22,000,000 Stock (raw cotton, yarn, packaging): KES 24,000,000 Smoke damage to administration block (est.): KES 1,000,000 --------------------------------------------------------------- Total Claimed: KES 85,000,000 5. SUPPORTING DOCUMENTS ENCLOSED

[X] Copy of Policy Schedule [X] Fire Brigade attendance confirmation (verbal, written report awaited) [ ] Fire investigation report - NOT YET RECEIVED, requested from independent loss adjuster, expected within 10 working days [X] Photographs of the affected areas (24 images) [ ] Stock records / inventory as at date of loss - PARTIALLY PROVIDED, warehouse stock ledger for July 2026 provided; August entries not yet reconciled [ ] Invoices for machinery being claimed as total loss - NOT YET PROVIDED [X] Maintenance/service record for fire extinguishers (last serviced March 2026) [ ] Maintenance/service record for sprinkler system in dye house - REQUESTED, NOT
arch 2026) [ ] Maintenance/service record for sprinkler system in dye house - REQUESTED, NOT YET RECEIVED [X] Statement from night shift supervisor (Mr
. Peter Kamau) [X] List of previous claims under this Policy (see Section 6)

6. PREVIOUS CLAIMS UNDER THIS POLICY (as declared by Insured) - March 2024: Minor fire, electrical fault in weaving section. Claimed KES 1,200,000. Settled KES 950,000. - November 2024: Water damage from burst pipe in warehouse. Claimed KES 2,800,000. Settled KES 2,400,000. - No other claims declared in the preceding 5 years. 7. INSURED'S DECLARATION I confirm that the information given above is true to the best of my knowledge.
I understand that the Insurer's liability is subject to the terms, conditions,
exclusions and warranties of the Policy. Signed: J. Wanjiru (Finance Director, Mavuno Textiles Limited)
Date: 5 August 2026

Signed: J. Wanjiru (Finance Director, Mavuno Textiles Limited)
Date: 5 August 2026 8. INTERNAL NOTE - AMANI GENERAL INSURANCE CLAIMS DEPARTMENT Given the estimated gross loss of KES 85,000,000, this claim falls above the
Cedant's retention of KES 50,000,000 under Treaty KR/AGI/SUR/2026 and has been
notified to Kenya Reinsurance Corporation Limited on 6 August 2026, within the
14-day notification period. Fire investigation report and sprinkler system
maintenance records are outstanding and have been requested from the Insured.
Cause of the fire (accidental electrical/mechanical fault vs. other cause) is not
yet confirmed pending the independent investigation report.

INDEPENDENT FIRE INVESTIGATION REPORT Prepared by: Ridgeway Loss Adjusters & Assessors Ltd
Report Reference: RWA/FIRE/2026/0341
For: Amani General Insurance Company Limited
Re: Mavuno Textiles Limited - Plot 14, Kariobangi Industrial Area, Nairobi
Claim Reference: AGI/CLM/2026/1187
Date of Report: 20 August 2026
Date of Site Inspection: 8 August 2026 1. INSTRUCTIONS We were instructed by Amani General Insurance Company Limited to attend the site,
investigate the cause and origin of the fire of 3 August 2026, and to comment on
the extent of loss and the condition of fire protection systems at the time of the
incident. 2. FINDINGS - CAUSE AND ORIGIN

2.1 Physical examination of the fire scene indicates the fire originated in the dye house, in the vicinity of Dyeing Vat No. 3, close to an electrical distribution panel serving the dye house boiler.
2.2 Char patterns and burn depth analysis are consistent with an electrical fault at or near the distribution panel as the most probable ignition source. We found no physical evidence of accelerant use, forced entry, or any indicator consistent with deliberate ignition.
2.3 The fire then spread rapidly into the adjoining warehouse through an open connecting doorway

. The warehouse contained loosely stored cotton lint and packaging materials, which are highly combustible and contributed materially to the speed of fire spread.
2.4 In our professional opinion, the most probable cause of the fire is accidental, arising from an electrical fault, with rapid spread aided by combustible material storage practices in the warehouse. We are unable to entirely rule out alternative causes given the extent of destruction in the immediate vicinity of the point of origin, but no evidence was found to support any cause other than accidental electrical fault.
3. FINDINGS - FIRE PROTECTION SYSTEMS

3.1 Sprinkler System: We requested maintenance and inspection records for the automatic sprinkler system covering the dye house and warehouse, as required under Warranty 1(a) of the Policy. At the time of our inspection, the Insured was unable to produce a maintenance record for the preceding 9 months. Visual inspection of sprinkler heads recovered from the debris in the dye house showed at least 3 heads that appeared to have been painted over, which can impair activation

. We recommend the Insurer request the full maintenance history directly from the service contractor named by the Insured (Safeguard Fire Systems Ltd) to establish whether the system was in good working order at the time of loss.
3.2 Portable Extinguishers: Service tags confirmed extinguishers were serviced in March 2026, consistent with the Insured's declaration and within policy requirements.
3.3 Housekeeping: We noted that cotton lint and packaging offcuts were stored in open areas of the warehouse rather than in the fire-resistant bins specified under Warranty 2 of the Policy, and were located significantly closer to the production floor than the 15-metre
of the Policy, and were located significantly closer to the production floor than the 15-metre separation specified

. This is a probable contributing factor to the speed and extent of fire spread, though it did not, in our assessment, cause the fire's ignition.
3.4 Fire Hydrant System: Found to be in working order and was used by the Nairobi County Fire Brigade during firefighting operations.
4. ESTIMATED EXTENT OF LOSS (Adjuster's Preliminary Assessment)

Buildings (dye house - total loss; warehouse - substantial damage): Adjuster estimate: KES 34,500,000 Plant and Machinery (dyeing vats, boiler, ancillary equipment): Adjuster estimate: KES 19,800,000 Stock (raw cotton, yarn, packaging - warehouse contents): Adjuster estimate, pending final stock reconciliation: KES 21,000,000 to 24,000,000 Smoke damage to administration block: Adjuster estimate: KES 650,000 --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Preliminary Adjuster Estimate (Total): KES 76,000,000 to 79,000,000

This preliminary estimate is below the Insured's own claimed figure of
KES 85,000,000, principally due to differences in the assessed value of destroyed
stock, which remains subject to final reconciliation against stock records once
the August ledger entries are made available. 5. OBSERVATIONS RELEVANT TO POLICY WARRANTIES

5. OBSERVATIONS RELEVANT TO POLICY WARRANTIES We note for the Insurer's consideration that the apparent lapse in sprinkler
system maintenance (Warranty 1(a)) and the housekeeping practices observed
(Warranty 2) may be relevant to the question of warranty compliance. We are not
qualified to opine on the legal effect of any breach; this is a matter for the
Insurer's claims and legal assessment. We can confirm, however, that the fire
protection deficiencies noted above are, in our professional opinion, more likely
than not to have contributed to the extent of the loss, even though they are not
assessed as the cause of ignition. 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

6. RECOMMENDATIONS 1. Obtain the full sprinkler maintenance history from Safeguard Fire Systems Ltd directly. 2. Obtain finalised stock ledger entries for August 2026 to confirm stock loss. 3. Obtain invoices or asset register entries for machinery claimed as a total loss to substantiate the claimed value. 4. We consider the claim, subject to the above outstanding items and the Insurer's own assessment of warranty compliance, to be a genuine loss arising from an accidental cause. Prepared by: S. Mutiso, Senior Loss Adjuster, Ridgeway Loss Adjusters & Assessors Ltd
